overview: Crackington Haven is a dramatic little cove between Bude and Boscastle, wedged between high cliffs at the end of a steep valley. The rocks here are famous: the cliffs are full of tightly folded layers of sandstone and shale, so much so that geologists named the Crackington Formation after the village.
At high tide the foreshore is stony, but as the tide drops a sandy beach is revealed. There’s a pub, a couple of tea rooms, toilets, and lifeguards in summer.

expect.title: The beach
expect.text: Stony at high water, sandy at low tide.

expect.title: The cliffs
expect.text: Look for the zig-zag folds in the rock layers on the cliffs around the cove.

expect.title: Cambeak
expect.text: A short walk south along the coast path leads to the Cambeak headland, with the clifftop at more than 300 feet.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: Two tea rooms, the Coombe Barton Inn and toilets near the beach.

goodToKnow.label: Leave the stones
goodToKnow.text: Signs ask visitors not to take stones from the beach; it’s an offence under coastal protection law.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About seven miles south-south-west of Bude and four miles north-north-east of Boscastle.

week.text: Go around low tide for the sand. It’s a good stop on a north-coast day between Bude and Boscastle, with a clifftop walk to stretch your legs afterwards.

pairWith.why: a big sandy surf beach towards Bude
a pretty harbour village to the south

tips: Check the tide times: the sandy beach only shows at lower tides.
